target_customer: Teams at Series A and B companies with 10 or more employees that work with AI agents daily
problem: Context from meetings, Slack and agent sessions is scattered, so agents and teammates lack shared memory.
business_model: Per-seat SaaS, $150 per team member per month after a 7-day trial per the website
product_category: Shared memory and company brain for AI agents (MCP)

founders.name: Diwank Tomer
previous_startups: AI company powering phone ordering for Domino's, Wingstop and Buffalo Wild Wings (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Directories give his surname as Singh in one place; YC lists Tomer. Education per YC page.

founders.name: Ishita Jindal
previous_startups: Julep AI (open source agent orchestrator, 7K+ GitHub stars)

competitors.name: Mem0
competitors.what: Long-term memory layer for AI apps

competitors.name: Supermemory
competitors.what: Memory engine; launched a Company Brain product later discontinued

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting Slack, Gmail and meeting tools, synthesizing living briefs and serving MCP tools with retrieval and permissions is standard LLM engineering; the team has prior open-source memory work.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated team memory may lock in, but model labs, Glean-style tools and several funded memory startups offer similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Supermemory discontinued its Company Brain product while keeping its memory engine; no incumbent action against Memory Store found.

market_need_then: Agents lack shared context; many memory startups raised in 2025 and 2026 (Mem0, Cognee, Sentra, Engram), indicating investor demand.

branding.domain_note: memory.store redirects (HTTP 301) to mem.store, where the site calls the product MemStore.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, plain and candid: 'Check in, record, recall.'

branding.brand_signature: The three-verb workflow check in, record, recall.

rebrands.why: A third-party page says the public brand shifted from Julep; the founders say memory was the bottleneck they kept seeing. No official announcement found, so this is unconfirmed.

branding.community_and_virality: Julep open source community (7K+ GitHub stars per the YC launch post).

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and clear but generic name that collides with many 'memory' and 'brain' products; evidence of brand pull is limited to the Julep open source audience.

pivots.why: Founders say memory was the recurring bottleneck across agents they saw at Julep; date not given.

outcome_analysis: Memory Store is a Spring 2026 YC company from founders who built the open-source Julep, still active and pre-outcome. It has real agent-infrastructure experience and a clear per-seat price. The category is crowded, with funded rivals and at least one competitor shutting a company-brain product, so defensibility against labs and incumbents is the open question.
notes: VCBacked lists a pre-seed in June 2026 (last funding June 16, 2026) from Y Combinator and Rebel Fund with no amount; FundedIQ reports $500K for the same date. Both are aggregators and single-sourced, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Founder name differs between YC (Tomer) and a directory (Singh).
